BuildCoverageResponse.description:
What one build contains, measured against the catalog it was drawn from (ADR 0033).

Bounded by construction: the payload is bounded by the axes and their limits, never by the
episode count. Read-only - no coverage figure takes part in a build's identity and no build
is refused for a gap.
BuildCoverageResponse.title: BuildCoverageResponse

BuildDetailResponse.description: A build plus the manifest and membership it is reproducible from.
BuildDetailResponse.title: BuildDetailResponse

BuildPayload.description:
A dataset build over a named selection of episodes (FR-006).

Empty `episode_ids` means "every episode that passed validation" - the
selection a first build almost always wants, and the one that is safe to
default to because a failing episode is excluded rather than silently
included.
BuildPayload.title: BuildPayload

BuildRedundancyResponse.description:
Near-duplicate structure of a build's membership (ADR 0032).

Read-only: the report proposes which episodes are the same behaviour recorded twice and
never removes one. `incomparable` lists the episodes that carry no signal to compare on
(no clock, no judged dimension) - they are counted as distinct, which is the honest
direction, and they are named so the count is not mistaken for a measurement.
BuildRedundancyResponse.title: BuildRedundancyResponse

ClusterProposal.description: One proposal. `frozen` is derived from a confirmation existing, never stored twice.
ClusterProposal.title: ClusterProposal

ClusterRun.description: One rebuild, with the health numbers that say whether to trust it.
ClusterRun.title: ClusterRun

ContractRequest.description: A declared expectation for one run. Every field is optional; all absent = no-op.
ContractRequest.title: ContractRequest

CoverageAxisResponse.description:
One axis of a build's coverage: what the build holds, and what it lacks (ADR 0033).

`missing` is the number of gaps before `gaps` was truncated, so a capped list reads as "at
least this many" rather than as the whole answer. The task axis's gaps are vocabulary
labels, so a label with no episode anywhere is a gap; every other axis's gaps are the
catalog's values the build left out.
CoverageAxisResponse.title: CoverageAxisResponse

CoverageValueResponse.description: One value on one coverage axis, with how much of the build it accounts for.
CoverageValueResponse.title: CoverageValueResponse

EpisodeExportResponse.description: Curated episode manifest: content identity, state, and quality per row.
EpisodeExportResponse.title: EpisodeExportResponse

EpisodeQualityResponse.description: Motion-quality and temporal-integrity signals for one episode (ADR 0018).
EpisodeQualityResponse.title: EpisodeQualityResponse

EpisodeSummary.description: Row in the episodes catalog; quality columns are null pre-analysis.
EpisodeSummary.title: EpisodeSummary

FailingEpisodeRow.description: One quarantined episode with its current failed validation result.
FailingEpisodeRow.title: FailingEpisodeRow

FailureSummaryResponse.description: Read-only aggregate of what is failing across episodes and profiles.
FailureSummaryResponse.title: FailureSummaryResponse

IncidentPayload.description: One incident. ``evidence`` is never empty: triage rejects uncited signals.
IncidentPayload.title: IncidentPayload

IncidentSummaryResponse.description: Queue shape, so a header can render severity counts without listing incidents.
IncidentSummaryResponse.title: IncidentSummaryResponse

JobReportEpisodes.description: State and motion-quality rollup of the episodes one run produced.
JobReportEpisodes.title: JobReportEpisodes

JobReportResponse.description: Run triage card: what a job produced, how it validates, how it moves.
JobReportResponse.title: JobReportResponse

JobReportValidation.description: Validation verdicts over the episodes one run produced.
JobReportValidation.title: JobReportValidation

JobSummary.description: Row in the jobs list; the full payload is available on the detail endpoint.
JobSummary.title: JobSummary

MetricSeriesPoint.description: One sparkline point: bucketed mean across the metric's label sets.
MetricSeriesPoint.title: MetricSeriesPoint

MetricSummaryModel.description: Descriptive statistics for one (metric, labels) sample set (ADR 0017).
MetricSummaryModel.title: MetricSummaryModel

MetricsResponse.description: Aggregated runtime telemetry read back from the JSONL metrics sink.
MetricsResponse.title: MetricsResponse

MonitoringHealthResponse.description: The monitor's own state. A monitor that silently stops is the worst outcome.
MonitoringHealthResponse.title: MonitoringHealthResponse

QualitySummaryResponse.description: Dataset-level distributions and outlier lists for curation triage.
QualitySummaryResponse.title: QualitySummaryResponse

QueueCursor.description: Continuation position in the ranked queue: pass back as after_* params.
QueueCursor.title: QueueCursor

RedundantEpisode.description: One episode a redundancy report would collapse into a group's representative.
RedundantEpisode.title: RedundantEpisode

SliceImpactResponse.description:
What a curation slice keeps and drops versus the whole dataset, and why.

`kept` and `dropped` partition the dataset and carry the same quality
signals for each side, so "this slice is smoother than what it dropped" is
a readable claim rather than an inference. `drop_reasons` attributes each
dropped episode to the first predicate it failed; `reorders_only` is the
honest zero: `short`/`long` order the view and exclude nothing.
SliceImpactResponse.title: SliceImpactResponse

SliceManifestResponse.description: Same manifest shape as the episodes export endpoint, but for one saved slice.
SliceManifestResponse.title: SliceManifestResponse

SlicePayload.description: Common fields for a saved slice.
SlicePayload.title: SlicePayload

SourceIngestPayload.description: A real episode on disk, described by path rather than by body.
SourceIngestPayload.title: SourceIngestPayload

StatusResponse.description: Backs the Status page: health, queue depth, and host telemetry.
StatusResponse.title: StatusResponse

TickResponse.description: One evaluation tick, for the on-demand endpoint and for tests.
TickResponse.title: TickResponse

ValidatePayload.description:
Which episodes to check, against which policy.

An empty `episode_ids` means "everything currently ingested" - the common
case after a bulk ingest, and an explicit statement rather than a default
that silently changes meaning if a caller forgets the field.

The policy travels as a whole document, not a name to look up. A job is a
self-contained, retryable record: if the profile is edited between the
submission and the attempt, the job must still validate against what was
asked for, not against whatever the name resolves to now.
ValidatePayload.title: ValidatePayload

ValidationResultResponse.description: One profile's verdict against one episode (ADR 0016).
ValidationResultResponse.title: ValidationResultResponse

VocabularyCandidate.description: One ranked suggestion. A suggestion is a queue item, never an action.
VocabularyCandidate.title: VocabularyCandidate

VocabularyEntry.description: One curated activity. The id is stable; the label is what a human approved.
VocabularyEntry.title: VocabularyEntry

VocabularyHealth.description: The numbers the page leads with; unmapped share is the headline (ADR 0029 §9).
VocabularyHealth.title: VocabularyHealth

VocabularyUnmappedRow.description: One novel task string - the bounded review queue's unit.
VocabularyUnmappedRow.title: VocabularyUnmappedRow

get.description:
Point a first-time visitor somewhere useful.

`/` is JSON rather than a redirect because a bare 404 in the browser was
the original complaint; the UI is one field away and the API callers get
the machine-readable map they expect.

Newest-first page of content-addressed artifacts with their referencing episodes.

``?format=csv|jsonl`` streams every artifact as a file download.

What this build contains, and what the catalog holds that it does not (ADR 0033).

Deterministic and read-only, computed from attributes ingest already wrote - task, robot,
format and verdict. The gap list is the actionable half: it names the values the catalog
holds and this build left out, and for tasks it names the vocabulary entries with no
episode here whether or not an episode exists for them anywhere.

The payload is bounded by the axes and their limits, never by the episode count, with
`missing` and `truncated` carrying what the caps left out.

Which episodes in this build are the same behaviour recorded twice (ADR 0032).

Deterministic and read-only, computed from signals ingest already wrote - no artifact
is opened and no model is involved. Membership is read in ordinal order and the rows
are put back into that order before the report runs, because truncation takes the
*first* N and a report whose coverage depended on a database's return order would not
be comparable between two runs.

An episode that was never scored has no fingerprint and is absent, so `episode_count`
is what was scored, not what the build holds.
Stored proposals with the health numbers of the run that produced them.
Current bounded triage queue and the latest human decisions.
One proposal and the task strings behind it.

Completion contracts, newest first.

``?format=csv|jsonl`` streams the filtered set as a download.

put.description:
Declare what a run is expected to produce; idempotent per job.

Re-declaring resets the outcome to pending, because a revised expectation
has not been evaluated yet and claiming otherwise would hide a breach.

get.description:
Scriptable episode catalog with the same curation views as the UI.

``?format=csv|jsonl`` streams every matching episode as a file download,
newest first.

Curated manifest for curation and dataset builds.

The same curation views as the catalog listing plus content identity
(source/artifact hashes). Registered before `/api/v1/episodes/{episode_id}`
so `export` is never read as an episode id.
The reverse lineage direction (FR-008): what contains this episode.
Motion-quality signals computed at ingest (ADR 0018).
Validation verdicts per profile: why an episode passed or was quarantined.
What is failing, how often, and under which profiles (read-only).

Quarantined episodes with the reason codes that put them there.

``?format=csv|jsonl`` streams the whole quarantined set as a download.

The incident queue, newest first. Read-only.

``?format=csv|jsonl`` streams the filtered queue as a download.

post.description: Acknowledge: an append-only fact, so a recurrence opens a new incident.
Resolve. A same-fault recurrence then opens a new incident, subject to cooldown.

get.description:
Newest-first page of jobs for the Jobs UI.

Cursor-based: pass the last item's ``created_at`` back as ``before``. The UI
never asks for every row. ``?format=csv|jsonl`` streams the whole filtered
set as a file download instead; ``limit``/``before`` page the JSON view only.

post.description:
Queue an ingest job.

Four request shapes, one endpoint: `ingest` carries an episode in the
request body (the synthetic contract), `ingest_source` names a dataset on
disk and lets a reader interpret it, `validate` and `build` name a
selection of episodes already in the catalog. They are separate types
rather than one optional payload because "either a body or a path" is
exactly the kind of either/or that a typo turns into a confusing 422.

Request cancellation (F7).

A queued job is canceled immediately; a running job moves to
`cancel_requested` and the worker stops it at its next checkpoint. A job that
already reached a terminal state cannot be cancelled (409), and an unknown id
is a 404.

get.description: Episodes this job produced, following lineage (run inspection).
Run triage card: what the run produced, how validation judged it, motion quality.

Aggregated runtime telemetry from the JSONL metrics sink.

Summaries describe every (metric, labels) sample set; series are bucketed
means per metric name for sparklines. Worker heartbeat age is derived from
the newest heartbeat record's timestamp, over all records rather than the
window (a dead worker must not vanish from a narrow window).

``?format=csv|jsonl`` downloads the sparkline series (metric, t, v,
count) for the same window.
The monitor's own state. A monitor that silently stops is the worst outcome.

What a notifier would send right now. Rendering only; nothing is sent.

Email delivery is deliberately not implemented (ADR 0020 §10.3): it needs
explicit owner authorization, and a dry run that is a real code path is the
only honest way to leave it switched off.

post.description:
Evaluate one window on demand.

The loop is a scheduler's job, not a webhook's; this exists so the notifier
can be driven deterministically from a test, a benchmark, or an operator who
wants to see what it would say right now.

Save a named curation filter.

Membership is recomputed on the next manifest read, so creating a slice is
cheap and the slice never goes stale as episodes change.

get.description: What the slice drops versus the whole dataset, and why (read-only).
The curated manifest for a saved slice: identity, state, quality.
Health, queue depth by state, entity counts, and host telemetry.
Status/Overview. The X-Fragment header returns only the polling body.

The client runtime. Served as a route rather than a static mount so the
UI stays one Python-owned directory with no extra file-serving surface.

Committed benchmark baselines and the runs recorded on this machine.

Reads `benchmarks/` off disk, so it needs no database and no catalog
table. A benchmark claim is a repository artifact, not a row.
Content-addressed builds. The address is the content.
One build, drawn as the graph lineage actually is.
Episode index with curation flags (jerky / stalled / short / long).
Every experiment record, indexed from its own metadata block.
Dataset curation view: distributions, variance heat, outlier lists.

post.description:
Queue a job from the browser form.

One front door, five kinds: `episode` and `path` are ingest, and `validate`,
`build` and `export` complete the loop those three form pages host (the audit's
release blocker 1 - EXP-0017 measured the last three steps as curl-only).

The form is parsed by hand rather than with ``Form(...)`` because that
would pull in ``python-multipart`` for a single urlencoded body - a new
dependency, on the dependency-free path ADR 0014 is built around, to save
three lines of ``urllib.parse``.

Every kind is built and then validated through the *same* Pydantic models
the JSON endpoint uses. A form is a second front door to the same door, and
a second front door with its own weaker validation is how a UI ends up able
to create jobs the API would refuse.

On a bad submission this re-renders the page that owns the form with the
error inline and the typed values preserved, rather than redirecting: losing
what someone typed because of one bad field is the fastest way to make a form
feel hostile. The redirect on success is 303, so a refresh does not queue the
same job twice.

Cancel from the UI and bounce back to the job.

A plain form post, so the control works without JavaScript. It calls the same
repository method as the API route rather than issuing an HTTP request to
ourselves; the redirect is 303 so a refresh does not re-submit the cancel.
